Flag the steps that are part of movement corridors

Source: R/event_flag_corridor.R
event_flag_corridor.Rd

This function detects corridors: places where animals move fast, in a consistent direction (either way along the corridor). It is a wrapper around move2utils::mt_corridor(), which requires the suggested package move2utils (install it with remotes::install_github("move2universe/move2utils")).

Usage

event_flag_corridor(
  x,
  speed_threshold = NULL,
  circvar_threshold = NULL,
  min_segments = 2
)

Arguments

x

A move2 object.

speed_threshold

The speed at or above which a step is fast, as a units object (e.g. as_units(1, "m/s")). Defaults to the upper quartile of the speeds of the steps.

circvar_threshold

A number between 0 and 1: the circular variance of the directions of the nearby steps at or below which they are considered to run in a similar direction. Defaults to the lower quartile of the circular variances.

min_segments

The minimum number of nearby steps (including the step itself) for a step to be part of a corridor.

Value

A logical vector with one value per event of x, TRUE for the events whose next step is part of a corridor (the last event of each track is FALSE).

Details

The nearby steps of a step (from an event to the next one in the same track) are the steps whose midpoints are within half its length of its midpoint, including the step itself. A step is a candidate if it is fast (speed_threshold), and if its nearby steps run in a similar direction (circvar_threshold). A step is then flagged as part of a corridor if it has at least min_segments nearby steps, and if more than half of them are candidates; a step that is not a candidate itself (e.g. a slow step) can therefore be flagged when it lies within a corridor.

When speed_threshold or circvar_threshold are not given, they are estimated from all the steps in x (pooling all tracks), with a warning giving the value used; give explicit values to compare corridors among datasets.

The search radius depends on the length of the steps, so it assumes roughly regular sampling; move2utils warns when the time intervals are very irregular.

x must be ordered by time within each track (see tt_order_time()). Events without a location are ignored, and get NA.

References

Based on the corridor() function of the move package, see LaPoint, S., Gallery, P., Wikelski, M. & Kays, R. (2013). Animal behavior, cost-based corridor models, and real corridors. Landscape Ecology, 28, 1615-1630. doi:10.1007/s10980-013-9910-0

Examples

event_flag_corridor(
  example_tt,
  speed_threshold = as_units(5, "m/s"),
  circvar_threshold = 0.5,
  min_segments = 1
)
#>  [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
#> [13] FALSE FALSE FALSE
